# D8_PARITY_FEAT_L8cfda948_20261110: per-bar feature table for L8cfda948 (tape block-print delta, b10_follow_sm L 50, z 1.0, sm 3, LONG only, bars row `dchg_40`), trading date 20261110, NY AM
Generated by W-D8SPEC2 (order 2200Z item 4). Research data only. Companion of autopilot/D8_PARITY_L8cfda948_20261110.md (bars, signals, trades). Times UTC with ms resolution.

## Definition (SPEC, engine code triggers_c/featc.py + core.py + defs.py)

- x = t_blk10_dlt per bar = sum over the individual MBO trade RECORDS of the day file whose ts_event lies in [t0, t1] of the bar (t0 = first print, t1 = last print of the bar; both ends inclusive) and whose SIZE >= 10 contracts, of (+size if the aggressor side flag is B, -size if A; records with side N count 0). Size is tested on each RECORD, not on a merged order.
- xs = ewm(span 3, adjust=False, ignore_na=True) of x over the continuous series of the row (all sessions in order); sd = rolling std (ddof 1) of xs over the last 50 bars, defined when at least max(5, 50 // 3) = 16 valid values exist; y = xs / sd; LONG when y >= 1.0 (SHORT when y <= -1.0, dropped: the cell trades long only); the signal is the edge of the condition; part = 1 bars never signal.
- Verified on this day: the per-record rule above reproduces the stored t_blk10_dlt on 104 of 109 NY AM bars; on 5 bars (bidx 40, 42, 63, 79, 91) my value differs from the stored one by 10 to 24 contracts (one block record more or less); the cause is NOT identified (OPEN; most likely a block record at a bar boundary where the engine uses the receive time of the print; not resolved). Recomputing xs, sd, y and the edge from the STORED x reproduces all 5,106 engine events (code/d8_spec2/feat_tables.py).

## How one aggressor order that fills several resting orders appears in the raw MBO trade records (SPEC from the day file, NQ_20261110.npz, NY AM 14:30-17:00 UTC)

- ONE RECORD PER RESTING ORDER FILLED. All records of one aggressor order carry the same ts_event (same nanosecond), the same aggressor side, and a sequence delta of 0 after the first; their prices step through the levels the order swept, and their sizes are the quantities filled against each resting order. Example (20261110 14:30:00.0028949 UTC, aggressor A = sell): records at 27743.00, 27742.75, 27742.50, each size 1.
- In NY AM of 20261110: 234,912 trade records; 206,616 distinct (ts_event, side) groups; 15,767 groups have more than one record (18.8% of all records); 14,429 of those groups span several prices (a sweep through levels) and 1,338 sit at a single price (several resting orders at one price).
- CONSEQUENCE for the block-print filter: records with size >= 10 are 270 (4,251 contracts) per record, but if the records of one aggressor order (same ts_event and side) were merged first, 1,641 groups reach >= 10 contracts (27,333 contracts): a 6-fold difference, and the per-bar x differs on 86 of the 109 NY AM bars. The engine feature uses the PER-RECORD rule (104 of 109 bars equal); a port that merges fills of one aggressor order, or that receives one tick per aggressor order, will compute a different x.
- NT8 / CQG: about 17% more trade ticks than the history tape for the same session (Josh export). How NT8 splits a sweep into ticks, and whether each tick is one resting-order fill, is NOT known to the engine side (OPEN): the port must be checked on this day by comparing x per bar below with the NT8 value computed from its own ticks (records with size >= 10 contracts, signed by aggressor), bar by bar.
